import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Is the minimum ropelength of a knot linear in its crossing number?

The *ropelength* of a closed curve $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is the scale-invariant ratio
$\operatorname{Len}(C)/\tau(C)$ of its length to its thickness. Following Gonzalez–Maddocks and
Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, the thickness $\tau(C)$ is the infimum of the radii of the circles
through three distinct points of $C$. It equals the radius of the largest embedded normal tube
around $C$. The ropelength $\operatorname{Rop}(K)$ of a knot type $K$ is the infimum of the
ropelength over all curves that realize $K$. The crossing number $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the
least number of crossings in a regular projection of a curve that realizes $K$.

Diao, Ernst, Por and Ziegler proved
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$.
The Wikipedia list of unsolved problems asks whether the upper bound is in fact linear:
is $\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$?

The unknot has crossing number $0$ and ropelength $2\pi > 0$, so the linear bound must allow an
additive constant. Since every nontrivial knot has crossing number at least $3$, this is the same
as a purely linear bound for nontrivial knots. Ropelength is measured in units of the thickness
radius; measuring in diameters halves it and does not affect the question.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [CKS02] Cantarella, J., Kusner, R. B., Sullivan, J. M., *On the minimum ropelength of knots and
  links*, Invent. Math. 150 (2002), 257–286. [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
- [DEPZ19] Diao, Y., Ernst, C., Por, A., Ziegler, U., *The ropelengths of knots are almost linear
  in terms of their crossing numbers*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019), 1950085.
-/

namespace IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

open scoped EuclideanGeometry unitInterval ENNReal NNReal

/-- A (closed) knot: a $C^1$ closed curve in $\mathbb{R}^3$ with nowhere vanishing derivative,
parametrised by $\mathbb{R}$ with period `1` and injective on each period. -/
structure IsKnot (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 γ
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv γ t ≠ 0
  injective : ∀ s t, γ s = γ t → ∃ n : ℤ, t = s + n

/-- Two closed curves are *ambient isotopic* (have the same knot type) if a continuous family of
homeomorphisms of $\mathbb{R}^3$ starting at the identity carries the image of the first onto the
image of the second. -/
def Isotopic (γ₀ γ₁ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : I → ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, Continuous (fun p : I × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' Set.range γ₀ = Set.range γ₁

/-- Every closed curve is ambient isotopic to itself, by the constant family of identities. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
lemma Isotopic.refl (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Isotopic γ γ :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, Set.image_id _⟩

/-- The length of one period of the closed curve `γ`. -/
noncomputable def length (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℝ := ∫ t in (0:ℝ)..1, ‖deriv γ t‖

/-- The *thickness* of the curve `γ` (Gonzalez–Maddocks, [CKS02, Section 2]): the infimum of the
circumradii of all non-degenerate triangles with vertices on the curve. Collinear triples of
points, which have infinite circumradius, do not contribute to the infimum. -/
noncomputable def thickness (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℝ :=
  ⨅ s : {s : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2 // ∀ i, s.points i ∈ Set.range γ}, s.1.circumradius

/-- The *ropelength* of the curve `γ`: its length divided by its thickness, measured in units of
the thickness radius. It is `∞` when the thickness is `0`. -/
noncomputable def curveRopelength (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ENNReal.ofReal (length γ) / ENNReal.ofReal (thickness γ)

/-- The (minimum) *ropelength* of the knot type of `γ`: the infimum of the ropelength over all
knots ambient isotopic to `γ`. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ' : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsKnot γ') (_ : Isotopic γ γ'), curveRopelength γ'

/-- The orthogonal projection of $\mathbb{R}^3$ onto the plane orthogonal to `u`. -/
noncomputable def proj (u : ℝ³) : ℝ³ →L[ℝ] ℝ³ := (ℝ ∙ u)ᗮ.starProjection

/-- The *crossings* of the projection of `γ` along `u`: the unordered pairs of distinct parameters
in one period whose projections coincide, encoded as pairs `(s, t)` with `0 ≤ s < t < 1`. -/
def crossings (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (u : ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | p.1 ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧ p.2 ∈ Set.Ico 0 1 ∧ p.1 < p.2 ∧
    proj u (γ p.1) = proj u (γ p.2)}

/-- The projection along the direction `u ≠ 0` is a *regular projection* of the knot `γ`: the
projected curve is regular (no tangent of `γ` is parallel to `u`), every point of the plane has
at most two preimages on the curve, the double points are transverse, and there are finitely many
of them. -/
structure IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) (u : ℝ³) : Prop where
  ne_zero : u ≠ 0
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, proj u (deriv γ t) ≠ 0
  encard_le_two : ∀ y, {t ∈ Set.Ico (0:ℝ) 1 | proj u (γ t) = y}.encard ≤ 2
  transverse : ∀ p ∈ crossings γ u,
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![proj u (deriv γ p.1), proj u (deriv γ p.2)]
  finite : (crossings γ u).Finite

/-- The *crossing number* of the knot type of `γ`: the least number of crossings in a regular
projection of a knot ambient isotopic to `γ`. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (γ' : ℝ → ℝ³) (_ : IsKnot γ') (_ : Isotopic γ γ') (u : ℝ³)
    (_ : IsRegularProjection γ' u), (crossings γ' u).encard

/-- Is the minimum ropelength of a closed knot bounded above by a linear function of its crossing
number? That is, are there constants $a, b$ such that every knot type $K$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) \le a \operatorname{Cr}(K) + b$? -/
@[category research open, AMS 51 53 57]
theorem is_the_upper_bound_of_a_closed_knots_minimum_ropelength_linear_to_its_crossing :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ a b : ℝ≥0, ∀ γ : ℝ → ℝ³, IsKnot γ →
      ropelength γ ≤ a * (crossingNumber γ : ℝ≥0∞) + b := by
  sorry

end IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

modeling_decisions: Knot type: a knot is a C¹ map γ : ℝ → ℝ³ with period 1, nowhere-vanishing derivative and injective modulo the period (a C¹ embedding of the circle); knot types are ambient isotopy classes of images (unoriented; a continuous family of homeomorphisms of ℝ³ starting at the identity carrying one image onto the other). C¹ knots are tame, so this ranges over exactly the tame knot types; both invariants are orientation- and mirror-independent so the choice of unoriented ambient isotopy does not change the claim.

Thickness: Gonzalez–Maddocks global radius of curvature as in CKS02 §2 — the infimum over all non-degenerate triangles (`Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2`) with vertices on the curve of their circumradius. Collinear triples (infinite radius in CKS) are omitted; they never affect the infimum. Measured as a radius, so the unknot has ropelength 2π (Wikipedia's convention). The real-valued `⨅` is 0 only in the unreachable case where the curve lies in a line.

Ropelength of a curve is ℝ≥0∞-valued: `ENNReal.ofReal length / ENNReal.ofReal thickness`, giving ∞ for zero thickness (matching CKS's 'finite ropelength' language) instead of Lean's real `x / 0 = 0`. Length is ∫₀¹ ‖γ'‖. Minimum ropelength of a knot type is the infimum over C¹ realizations; no loss since CKS show any curve of finite ropelength is C^{1,1}.

Crossing number is ℕ∞-valued: the infimum, over knots γ' isotopic to γ and directions u ≠ 0, of the number of crossings of a regular projection. A regular projection requires: u ≠ 0 (otherwise the projection is the identity and every knot would get crossing number 0), projected curve regular (no tangent parallel to u), every point of the plane has at most two preimages in one period (no triple points), transverse double points (linearly independent projected tangents), finitely many double points. Crossings are counted as pairs (s,t) with 0 ≤ s < t < 1 and equal projections. Requiring transversality/regularity is the literal textbook definition; the minimum over the isotopy class equals the classical crossing number.

Linearity is formalised as an affine bound `Rop ≤ a·Cr + b` with a, b : ℝ≥0 (coerced to ℝ≥0∞), i.e. big-O; the additive constant is needed for the unknot and, given Cr ≥ 3 for nontrivial knots, is equivalent to `∃ c, ∀ nontrivial K, Rop K ≤ c·Cr K`. Using ℝ≥0 rather than ℝ≥0∞ for a, b prevents the trivial witness a = ⊤.

Degenerate cases: if some knot type had no realization of positive thickness or no regular projection (impossible for tame knots), the ℝ≥0∞/ℕ∞ infima give ⊤, making the bound false rather than vacuously true; the only Lean default that is reached in a non-mathematical way is none. With a = 0 and Cr = ⊤ the ENNReal product is 0, but Cr = ⊤ is unreachable.

the ropelength over all curves realizing $K$.

The crossing number $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the least number of crossings in a knot diagram
of $K$, i.e. in a regular projection to a plane of a curve realizing $K$.

It is known that $\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$
(Diao–Ernst–Por–Ziegler), and that there are families of knots whose ropelength grows linearly
in the crossing number. The question asks whether the upper bound can be improved to a linear
one: is there a universal constant $c$ with $\operatorname{Rop}(K) \le c \operatorname{Cr}(K)$
for every nontrivial knot $K$?

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Crossing number (knot theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossing_number_(knot_theory))
- J. Cantarella, R. B. Kusner, J. M. Sullivan, *On the minimum ropelength of knots and links*,
  Invent. Math. 150 (2002), [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
- Y. Diao, C. Ernst, A. Por, U. Ziegler, *The ropelengths of knots are almost linear in terms of
  their crossing numbers*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019),
  [doi:10.1142/S0218216519500858](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218216519500858)
-/

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

namespace IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

/-- A ($C^1$) knot: a $1$-periodic $C^1$ map $\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ which is
injective on a period, so that it traces out a simple closed curve exactly once. -/
structure IsKnot (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 γ
  periodic : Function.Periodic γ 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1)

/-- Two subsets $A, B \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$ are *ambient isotopic* if there is a
level-preserving homeomorphism $F$ of $\mathbb{R}^3 \times [0, 1]$ which is the identity on the
level $t = 0$ and carries $A$ onto $B$ on the level $t = 1$. Two knots have the same knot type
exactly when their images are ambient isotopic. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (A B : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : ℝ³ × unitInterval ≃ₜ ℝ³ × unitInterval,
    (∀ p, (F p).2 = p.2) ∧ (∀ x, F (x, 0) = (x, 0)) ∧ (fun x => (F (x, 1)).1) '' A = B

/-- The *thickness* (Gonzalez–Maddocks global radius of curvature) of a set
$A \subseteq \mathbb{R}^3$: the infimum of the circumradii of all nondegenerate triangles
with vertices in $A$. For a $C^1$ closed curve this is the radius of the largest embedded normal
tube around the curve (Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, Lemma 2), and it is positive exactly when the
curve is a $C^{1,1}$ simple closed curve. -/
noncomputable def thickness (A : Set ℝ³) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ s : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2, (∀ i, s.points i ∈ A) ∧ s.circumradius = r}

/-- The length $\int_0^1 \|\gamma'(t)\| \, dt$ of one period of a $C^1$ closed curve
$\gamma : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ of period $1$. -/
noncomputable def length (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℝ :=
  ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ‖deriv γ t‖

/-- The (minimum) *ropelength* of the knot type of `γ₀`: the infimum of
$\operatorname{Len}(\gamma) / \tau(\gamma)$ over all knots `γ` of positive thickness that are
ambient isotopic to `γ₀`. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (γ₀ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℝ :=
  sInf {ρ | ∃ γ, IsKnot γ ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ₀) (Set.range γ) ∧
    0 < thickness (Set.range γ) ∧ ρ = length γ / thickness (Set.range γ)}

/-- The projection $\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^2$ along the third coordinate axis. -/
def proj (x : ℝ³) : ℝ² := !₂[x 0, x 1]

/-- The double points of the planar projection of a closed curve `γ` of period `1`: the points of
the plane that are hit by `proj ∘ γ` at two different parameters `s ≠ t` in `[0, 1)`. -/
def doublePoints (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p | ∃ s ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ t ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1,
    s ≠ t ∧ proj (γ s) = p ∧ proj (γ t) = p}

/-- The planar projection of the closed curve `γ` of period `1` is *regular*, i.e. it is a knot
diagram of `γ`: the projected curve is an immersion, no point of the plane is hit at three
different parameters in `[0, 1)`, and at every double point the two strands cross
transversally. -/
structure IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : Prop where
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv (proj ∘ γ) t ≠ 0
  no_triple_points : ∀ r ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ s ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1,
    ∀ t ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, proj (γ r) = proj (γ s) → proj (γ r) = proj (γ t) →
    r = s ∨ r = t ∨ s = t
  transverse : ∀ s ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, s ≠ t →
    proj (γ s) = proj (γ t) →
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![deriv (proj ∘ γ) s, deriv (proj ∘ γ) t]

/-- The *crossing number* of the knot type of `γ₀`: the least number of double points of a
regular projection (i.e. the least number of crossings of a knot diagram) of a knot ambient
isotopic to `γ₀`. Every tame knot type contains a knot whose projection is regular with finitely
many double points, and rotating a knot is an ambient isotopy, so it suffices to project along a
fixed direction. If `γ₀` is not tame, the set is empty and the value is `0` by convention. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ₀ : ℝ → ℝ³) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ γ, IsKnot γ ∧ AmbientIsotopic (Set.range γ₀) (Set.range γ) ∧
    IsRegularProjection γ ∧ (doublePoints γ).encard = n}

/-- Ambient isotopy is reflexive. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem ambientIsotopic_refl (A : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic A A :=
  ⟨Homeomorph.refl _, fun _ => rfl, fun _ => rfl, Set.image_id _⟩

/-- The thickness of a set is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 53]
theorem thickness_nonneg (A : Set ℝ³) : 0 ≤ thickness A := by
  apply Real.sInf_nonneg
  rintro r ⟨s, -, rfl⟩
  exact s.circumradius_nonneg

/-- The length of a closed curve is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 53]
theorem length_nonneg (γ : ℝ → ℝ³) : 0 ≤ length γ :=
  intervalIntegral.integral_nonneg zero_le_one fun _ _ => norm_nonneg _

/-- The ropelength of a knot is nonnegative. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
theorem ropelength_nonneg (γ₀ : ℝ → ℝ³) : 0 ≤ ropelength γ₀ := by
  apply Real.sInf_nonneg
  rintro ρ ⟨γ, -, -, hτ, rfl⟩
  exact div_nonneg (length_nonneg γ) hτ.le

/--
**Is the upper bound of a closed knot's minimum ropelength linear to its crossing number?**

Is there a universal constant $c$ such that
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) \le c \cdot \operatorname{Cr}(K)$ for every nontrivial (tame) knot type
$K$, where $\operatorname{Rop}(K)$ is the minimum ropelength and $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ the
crossing number of $K$? In other words, is $\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$?

Knot types are represented by a $C^1$ knot `γ` of positive thickness, i.e. a knot that can be
tied in rope (this is exactly the class of knots with finite ropelength; every tame knot type has
such a representative). The unknot is excluded, since it has crossing number $0$ but positive
ropelength, by requiring $\operatorname{Cr}(K) > 0$. Ropelength is measured in units of the
tube radius; the choice of units does not affect the question.

The best known upper bound is
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$
(Diao–Ernst–Por–Ziegler); a linear upper bound would be optimal, since there are families of
knots whose ropelength grows linearly in the crossing number.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem is_the_upper_bound_of_a_closed_knots_minimum_ropelength_linear_to_its_crossing :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ γ : ℝ → ℝ³,
      IsKnot γ → 0 < thickness (Set.range γ) → 0 < crossingNumber γ →
        ropelength γ ≤ c * crossingNumber γ := by
  sorry

end IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

CKS Lemma 2 shows this equals the radius of the largest embedded normal tube; ropelength is thus measured in units of the tube radius (the Wikipedia convention). Ropelength of a knot type is the infimum of `length γ / thickness (range γ)` over C¹ realizations `γ` with `0 < thickness`. /-- Three-dimensional Euclidean space. -/

/-- A regular $C^1$ parametrization of a closed knot. The parametrization has period one and is
injective modulo its period. -/
structure ClosedKnot where
  toFun : ℝ → Space
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 toFun
  periodic : Function.Periodic toFun 1
  injectiveModuloPeriod : ∀ {x y}, toFun x = toFun y → ∃ n : ℤ, y = x + n
  regular : ∀ x, fderiv ℝ toFun x 1 ≠ 0

instance : CoeFun ClosedKnot (fun _ ↦ ℝ → Space) := ⟨ClosedKnot.toFun⟩

/-- Two closed knots are ambient isotopic. Here `H` is the isotopy and `G` is its jointly
continuous inverse. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (K L : ClosedKnot) : Prop :=
  ∃ H G : ℝ → Space → Space,
    Continuous (Function.uncurry H) ∧ Continuous (Function.uncurry G) ∧
    (∀ x, H 0 x = x) ∧
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ x, G t (H t x) = x ∧ H t (G t x) = x) ∧
    H 1 '' Set.range K = Set.range L

/-- The length of one period of a closed knot, defined as the supremal length of its inscribed
polygons. -/
noncomputable def knotLength (K : ClosedKnot) : ℝ :=
  variationOnFromTo K Set.univ 0 1

/-- The thickness of a closed knot, defined as the reach of its image: the largest radius such
that every point at smaller distance from the knot has a unique nearest point on it. -/
noncomputable def thickness (K : ClosedKnot) : ℝ :=
  sSup {r : ℝ | 0 ≤ r ∧ ∀ x : Space, Metric.infDist x (Set.range K) < r →
    ∃! y : Space, y ∈ Set.range K ∧ dist x y = Metric.infDist x (Set.range K)}

/-- Orthogonal projection onto the plane perpendicular to a unit vector `u`. -/
noncomputable def planeProjection (u x : Space) : Space := x - inner ℝ u x • u

/-- Parameter pairs giving double points in the projection of `K` along `u`. Restricting to
$0 \le x < y < 1$ counts each unordered pair once. -/
def crossingPairs (K : ClosedKnot) (u : Space) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | 0 ≤ p.1 ∧ p.1 < p.2 ∧ p.2 < 1 ∧
    planeProjection u (K p.1) = planeProjection u (K p.2)}

/-- A regular knot projection has a unit projection direction, finitely many double points, no
triple points, and linearly independent projected tangent vectors at every double point. -/
def IsRegularProjection (K : ClosedKnot) (u : Space) : Prop :=
  ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ (crossingPairs K u).Finite ∧
    (∀ p ∈ crossingPairs K u, ∀ q ∈ crossingPairs K u, p.1 = q.1 → p.2 = q.2) ∧

all ambient-isotopic realizations. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : ClosedKnot) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ L : ClosedKnot, AmbientIsotopic K L ∧ ∃ u : Space,
    IsRegularProjection L u ∧ n = (crossingPairs L u).ncard}

positive-thickness, ambient-isotopic $C^1$ realizations. -/

  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ L : ClosedKnot, AmbientIsotopic K L ∧ 0 < thickness L ∧
    r = knotLength L / thickness L}

    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ K : ClosedKnot, crossingNumber K ≠ 0 →

  sorry

namespace IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

open Set
open scoped ENNReal NNReal Matrix RealInnerProductSpace unitInterval

abbrev Point3 := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/-- A parametrized tame closed knot: a regular `C¹`, `2π`-periodic curve which is injective on a
half-open fundamental interval. -/
structure ClosedKnot where
  toFun : ℝ → Point3
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 toFun
  periodic : Function.Periodic toFun (2 * Real.pi)
  injectiveOn : Set.InjOn toFun (Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi))
  regular : ∀ t, fderiv ℝ toFun t (1 : ℝ) ≠ 0

instance : FunLike ClosedKnot ℝ Point3 where
  coe := ClosedKnot.toFun
  coe_injective' f g h := by cases f; cases g; cases h; rfl

/-- Two parametrized knots have the same knot type when they are joined by an isotopy through
regular closed embeddings. This agrees with ambient isotopy by the isotopy extension theorem. -/
def Isotopic (f g : ClosedKnot) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : I → ClosedKnot,
    Continuous (fun p : I × ℝ ↦ F p.1 p.2) ∧
      (F 0 : ℝ → Point3) = f ∧ (F 1 : ℝ → Point3) = g

/-- The usual vector cross product in three-dimensional Euclidean space. -/
def cross (x y : Point3) : Point3 :=
  WithLp.toLp 2 (crossProduct (WithLp.ofLp x) (WithLp.ofLp y))

/-- The radius of the circle through three points, with value `∞` for collinear points. -/
def circumradius (x y z : Point3) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  if ‖cross (y - x) (z - x)‖ = 0 then ∞
  else ENNReal.ofReal (dist x y * dist y z * dist z x /
    (2 * ‖cross (y - x) (z - x)‖))

/-- Knot thickness, defined as the infimum of the circumradii through triples of distinct points
of the curve. -/
def thickness (f : ClosedKnot) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ x ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi),
    ∃ y ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi),
    ∃ z ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi),
      x ≠ y ∧ y ≠ z ∧ z ≠ x ∧ r = circumradius (f x) (f y) (f z)}

/-- The length of one traversal of a closed knot. -/
def length (f : ClosedKnot) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  eVariationOn f (Set.Icc 0 (2 * Real.pi))

/-- The ropelength of a realization is its length divided by its thickness. -/
def ropelength (f : ClosedKnot) : ℝ≥0∞ := length f / thickness f

/-- The minimum ropelength in the isotopy class of `f`. -/
def minimumRopelength (f : ClosedKnot) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sInf {r | ∃ g : ClosedKnot, Isotopic f g ∧ r = ropelength g}

/-- Orthogonal projection onto the plane perpendicular to `v`. -/
def projectPerp (v x : Point3) : Point3 := x - (inner ℝ x v • v)

/-- The unordered pairs of parameters which become double points under projection along `v`. -/
def crossingPairs (f : ClosedKnot) (v : Point3) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | p.1 ∈ Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi) ∧ p.2 ∈ Set.Ico 0 (2 * Real.pi) ∧ p.1 < p.2 ∧
    projectPerp v (f p.1) = projectPerp v (f p.2)}

/-- A projection direction is regular if it is a unit direction, the projected curve is immersed,
has finitely many double points, has no triple points, and the two projected tangents at every
double point are transverse. -/
def IsRegularProjection (f : ClosedKnot) (v : Point3) : Prop :=
  ‖v‖ = 1 ∧ (crossingPairs f v).Finite ∧
    (∀ t ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi),
      projectPerp v (fderiv ℝ f.toFun t 1) ≠ 0) ∧
    (∀ x ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi),
      ∀ y ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi),
      ∀ z ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) (2 * Real.pi),
        projectPerp v (f x) = projectPerp v (f y) →
        projectPerp v (f x) = projectPerp v (f z) → x = y ∨ x = z ∨ y = z) ∧
    ∀ p ∈ crossingPairs f v,
      cross (projectPerp v (fderiv ℝ f.toFun p.1 1))
        (projectPerp v (fderiv ℝ f.toFun p.2 1)) ≠ 0

/-- The crossing number of a knot type: the minimum number of crossings among all regular
projections of all isotopic realizations. -/
def crossingNumber (f : ClosedKnot) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ g : ClosedKnot, Isotopic f g ∧
    ∃ v : Point3, IsRegularProjection g v ∧ n = (crossingPairs g v).ncard}

but whose minimum ropelength is positive. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]

      minimumRopelength f ≤ (c : ℝ≥0∞) * (crossingNumber f : ℝ≥0∞) := by
  sorry

# Ropelength and crossing number

- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)

namespace IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

open scoped ENNReal

abbrev Point := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

/--
A regular period-one parametrized closed $C^1$ knot. Injectivity is imposed on one half-open
period, and regularity means that the velocity never vanishes.
-/
def IsKnotCurve (γ : ℝ → Point) : Prop :=
  ContDiff ℝ 1 γ ∧ Function.Periodic γ 1 ∧ Set.InjOn γ (Set.Ico 0 1) ∧
    ∀ t, fderiv ℝ γ t 1 ≠ 0

/-- The contour length of one period of a closed curve. -/
noncomputable def curveLength (γ : ℝ → Point) : ℝ :=
  (eVariationOn γ (Set.Icc 0 1)).toReal

/--
The thickness of a curve, defined as its reach: the supremum of the radii for which every
point at distance less than the radius has a unique nearest point on the curve.
For $C^1$ knots this equals the radius of the largest embedded normal tube.
-/
noncomputable def thickness (γ : ℝ → Point) : ℝ :=
  sSup {r : ℝ | 0 ≤ r ∧ ∀ p : Point, Metric.infDist p (Set.range γ) < r →
    ∃! q : Point, q ∈ Set.range γ ∧ dist p q = Metric.infDist p (Set.range γ)}

/-- Two parametrized knots are isotopic through a continuous family of $C^1$ knot curves. -/
def Isotopic (γ η : ℝ → Point) : Prop :=
  ∃ F : ℝ × ℝ → Point, Continuous F ∧
    (∀ s, F (0, s) = γ s) ∧ (∀ s, F (1, s) = η s) ∧
    ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, IsKnotCurve (fun s ↦ F (t, s))

/-- The minimum ropelength in the knot type represented by `γ`. -/
noncomputable def minimumRopelength (γ : ℝ → Point) : ℝ :=
  sInf {r : ℝ | ∃ η : ℝ → Point, Isotopic γ η ∧ 0 < thickness η ∧
    r = curveLength η / thickness η}

/-- Orthogonal projection to the plane perpendicular to a unit vector `v`. -/
noncomputable def projectPerp (v x : Point) : Point := x - inner ℝ x v • v

/-- Ordered parameter pairs which form crossings in the projection along `v`. -/
def projectionCrossings (γ : ℝ → Point) (v : Point) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | p.1 ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ p.2 ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1 ∧ p.1 < p.2 ∧
    projectPerp v (γ p.1) = projectPerp v (γ p.2)}

/--
A regular knot projection: the projected curve is an immersion, it has finitely many double
points, every double point has exactly two preimages, and all crossings are transverse.
-/
def IsRegularProjection (γ : ℝ → Point) (v : Point) : Prop :=
  (∀ t ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, projectPerp v (fderiv ℝ γ t 1) ≠ 0) ∧
  (projectionCrossings γ v).Finite ∧
  ∀ p ∈ projectionCrossings γ v,
    (∀ u ∈ Set.Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, projectPerp v (γ u) = projectPerp v (γ p.1) →
      u = p.1 ∨ u = p.2) ∧
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![
      projectPerp v (fderiv ℝ γ p.1 1), projectPerp v (fderiv ℝ γ p.2 1)]

/-- The crossing number of the knot type represented by `γ`. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (γ : ℝ → Point) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ (η : ℝ → Point) (v : Point), Isotopic γ η ∧ ‖v‖ = 1 ∧
    IsRegularProjection η v ∧ n = (projectionCrossings η v).ncard}

/--
Is there a universal linear upper bound for minimum ropelength in terms of crossing number?
Precisely, does there exist $c>0$ such that every nontrivial tame closed knot type $K$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) \leq c\,\operatorname{Cr}(K)$? Here knot types are represented by closed
$C^1$ curves, thickness is measured in units of tube radius, and nontriviality is expressed by
positive crossing number (excluding the unknot, whose crossing number is zero).
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem is_the_upper_bound_of_a_closed_knots_minimum_ropelength_linear_to_its_crossing :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ γ : ℝ → Point, IsKnotCurve γ →
      0 < crossingNumber γ → minimumRopelength γ ≤ c * crossingNumber γ := by
  sorry

end IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

/-!
# Is the upper bound of a closed knot's minimum ropelength linear to its crossing number?

The *ropelength* of a curve $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is $\operatorname{Len}(C)/\tau(C)$, the
quotient of its length by its thickness. The (minimum) ropelength $\operatorname{Rop}(K)$ of a
knot type $K$ is the infimum of the ropelength over all curves realizing $K$. It is known that
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K)\log^5\operatorname{Cr}(K))$, where
$\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the crossing number, and it is conjectured that the tight upper bound
is linear in the crossing number.

Following Gonzalez–Maddocks and Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, the thickness of a curve is the
infimal radius of a circle through three distinct points of the curve (the tube *radius*).
Length is the one-dimensional Hausdorff measure of the curve. The crossing number is the least
number of crossings in a regular projection of a polygonal representative of the knot type, so it
is only meaningful for tame knots.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Wikipedia, Crossing number (knot theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossing_number_(knot_theory))
- [CKS02] Cantarella, J., Kusner, R. B., Sullivan, J. M.,
  _On the minimum ropelength of knots and links_. Invent. Math. 150 (2002), 257–286.
  [arXiv:math/0103224](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0103224)
- [DEPZ19] Diao, Y., Ernst, C., Por, A., Ziegler, U.,
  _The ropelengths of knots are almost linear in terms of their crossing numbers_.
  J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019), 1950085.
-/

namespace IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

open MeasureTheory
open scoped EuclideanGeometry ENNReal NNReal unitInterval

/- ### Knots and ambient isotopy -/

/-- A (closed) **knot** is a subset of `ℝ³` homeomorphic to a circle. -/
def IsKnot (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  Nonempty (K ≃ₜ Circle)

/-- Two subsets `K₀`, `K₁` of `ℝ³` are **ambient isotopic** if there is a continuous family
`H t` (`t ∈ [0, 1]`) of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0` the identity and
`H 1 '' K₀ = K₁`. The knot type of a knot is its ambient isotopy class. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (K₀ K₁ : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : I → ℝ³ ≃ₜ ℝ³, Continuous (fun p : I × ℝ³ => H p.1 p.2) ∧
    H 0 = Homeomorph.refl ℝ³ ∧ H 1 '' K₀ = K₁

/-- The closed polygon with consecutive vertices `v 0, v 1, …, v (n - 1)` (and `v (n - 1)` joined
back to `v 0`). -/
def closedPolygon {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → ℝ³) : Set ℝ³ :=
  ⋃ i, segment ℝ (v i) (v (finRotate n i))

/-- A knot is **tame** if it is ambient isotopic to a closed polygon. -/
def IsTame (K : Set ℝ³) : Prop :=
  ∃ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → ℝ³), AmbientIsotopic K (closedPolygon v)

/-- The standard **unknot**: the unit circle in the `xy`-plane. -/
def unknot : Set ℝ³ :=
  Metric.sphere (0 : ℝ³) 1 ∩ {x | x 2 = 0}

/- ### Thickness and ropelength -/

open scoped Classical in
/-- The radius of the circle through three points of `ℝ³`, defined to be `∞` when the three
points are not affinely independent (i.e. are collinear or not distinct). -/
noncomputable def circumradius (x y z : ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  if h : AffineIndependent ℝ ![x, y, z] then
    ENNReal.ofReal (⟨![x, y, z], h⟩ : Affine.Triangle ℝ ℝ³).circumradius
  else ⊤

/-- The **thickness** of a curve `K ⊆ ℝ³` is the infimal radius of a circle through three
distinct points of `K` (Gonzalez–Maddocks; [CKS02, Section 2]). For a `C¹` curve this is the
radius of the largest embedded normal tube around `K`; positive thickness forces `K` to be
`C^{1,1}` [CKS02, Section 3]. -/
noncomputable def thickness (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (x ∈ K) (y ∈ K) (z ∈ K) (_ : x ≠ y) (_ : x ≠ z) (_ : y ≠ z), circumradius x y z

/-- The **ropelength** of a curve `K ⊆ ℝ³`: its length (one-dimensional Hausdorff measure)
divided by its thickness. -/
noncomputable def ropelength (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  μH[1] K / thickness K

/-- The **minimum ropelength** $\operatorname{Rop}(K)$ of the knot type of `K`: the infimum of the
ropelength over all curves ambient isotopic to `K`. Curves of thickness `0` have infinite
ropelength and are omitted from the infimum. -/
noncomputable def minRopelength (K : Set ℝ³) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (K' : Set ℝ³) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K K') (_ : 0 < thickness K'), ropelength K'

/- ### Crossing number -/

/-- Orthogonal projection of `ℝ³` onto the `xy`-plane. -/
def proj (x : ℝ³) : ℝ² :=
  !₂[x 0, x 1]

/-- The **double points** of the projection of `K ⊆ ℝ³` onto the `xy`-plane: points of the
plane with at least two preimages in `K`. -/
def doublePoints (K : Set ℝ³) : Set ℝ² :=
  {p | ∃ x ∈ K, ∃ y ∈ K, x ≠ y ∧ proj x = p ∧ proj y = p}

/-- The projection of the closed polygon with vertices `v` onto the `xy`-plane is **regular**
(i.e. is a knot diagram) if it has only finitely many multiple points, all of which are double
points, and no vertex projects onto a double point. -/
structure IsRegularProjection {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → ℝ³) : Prop where
  finite : (doublePoints (closedPolygon v)).Finite
  encard_le : ∀ p : ℝ², (closedPolygon v ∩ proj ⁻¹' {p}).encard ≤ 2
  vertex_notMem : ∀ i, proj (v i) ∉ doublePoints (closedPolygon v)

/-- The **crossing number** $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ of the knot type of `K`: the least number of
double points in a regular projection of a closed polygon ambient isotopic to `K`. Since
rotations of `ℝ³` are ambient isotopies, it suffices to project onto the `xy`-plane. This is
`⊤` when `K` is not tame. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Set ℝ³) : ℕ∞ :=
  ⨅ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → ℝ³) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K (closedPolygon v))
    (_ : IsRegularProjection v), ((doublePoints (closedPolygon v)).ncard : ℕ∞)

/- ### Basic API -/

/-- Ambient isotopy is reflexive. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem AmbientIsotopic.refl (K : Set ℝ³) : AmbientIsotopic K K :=
  ⟨fun _ => Homeomorph.refl ℝ³, continuous_snd, rfl, Set.image_id K⟩

/-- The thickness of a curve is at most the radius of any circle through three of its points. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem thickness_le_circumradius {K : Set ℝ³} {x y z : ℝ³} (hx : x ∈ K) (hy : y ∈ K)
    (hz : z ∈ K) (hxy : x ≠ y) (hxz : x ≠ z) (hyz : y ≠ z) :
    thickness K ≤ circumradius x y z :=
  iInf₂_le_of_le x hx <| iInf₂_le_of_le y hy <| iInf₂_le_of_le z hz <|
    iInf_le_of_le hxy <| iInf_le_of_le hxz <| iInf_le _ hyz

/-- The minimum ropelength of a knot type is at most the ropelength of any of its realizations of
positive thickness. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem minRopelength_le {K K' : Set ℝ³} (h : AmbientIsotopic K K') (h' : 0 < thickness K') :
    minRopelength K ≤ ropelength K' :=
  iInf₂_le_of_le K' h <| iInf_le _ h'

/-- The crossing number of a knot type is at most the number of double points of any regular
projection of a closed polygon realizing it. -/
@[category API, AMS 57]
theorem crossingNumber_le {K : Set ℝ³} {n : ℕ} {v : Fin n → ℝ³}
    (h : AmbientIsotopic K (closedPolygon v)) (hv : IsRegularProjection v) :
    crossingNumber K ≤ (doublePoints (closedPolygon v)).ncard :=
  iInf₂_le_of_le n v <| iInf₂_le h hv

/- ### The conjecture -/

/--
**Is the upper bound of a closed knot's minimum ropelength linear to its crossing number?**

Is there a constant $c$ such that every nontrivial tame knot $K$ satisfies
$$\operatorname{Rop}(K) \le c \cdot \operatorname{Cr}(K),$$
i.e. is $\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$? Here $\operatorname{Rop}(K)$ is the
minimum ropelength of $K$ and $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ its crossing number. The best known bound is
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$ [DEPZ19].

The unknot is excluded since it has crossing number $0$ but ropelength $2\pi$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 51 57]
theorem is_the_upper_bound_of_a_closed_knots_minimum_ropelength_linear_to_its_crossing :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ≥0, ∀ K : Set ℝ³,
      IsKnot K → IsTame K → ¬ AmbientIsotopic K unknot →
        minRopelength K ≤ c * (crossingNumber K : ℝ≥0∞) := by
  sorry

end IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing

The *ropelength* of a closed curve $C$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is the scale-invariant ratio
$\operatorname{Len}(C) / \tau(C)$ of its length to its *thickness*. Following Gonzalez–Maddocks and
Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan, the thickness $\tau(C)$ is the infimum of the circumradius
$r(x, y, z)$ over all triples of distinct points of $C$; for smooth curves this is the radius of
the largest embedded normal tube around $C$. The *ropelength* $\operatorname{Rop}(K)$ of a knot
type $K$ is the infimum of the ropelength over all curves realizing $K$.

For every nontrivial knot $K$ one has $\operatorname{Rop}(K) \geq c \operatorname{Cr}(K)^{3/4}$,
and Diao, Ernst, Por and Ziegler proved the near-linear upper bound
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K) \log^5 \operatorname{Cr}(K))$, where
$\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ is the crossing number. It is conjectured that the tight upper bound is
linear, i.e. that there is a universal constant $c$ with
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) \leq c \operatorname{Cr}(K)$ for every nontrivial knot $K$.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Ropelength](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ropelength)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

  their crossing numbers*, J. Knot Theory Ramifications 28 (2019)](https://doi.org/10.1142/S0218216519500858)

/-- A (tame) knot in $\mathbb{R}^3$: a $C^1$ embedding of the circle, given as a $1$-periodic
$C^1$ map `γ : ℝ → ℝ³` with nowhere-vanishing derivative that is injective on a period `[0, 1)`.
Every $C^1$ immersed embedded circle is a tame knot. -/
structure Knot where
  /-- The parametrization of the knot. -/
  toFun : ℝ → ℝ³
  periodic : Function.Periodic toFun 1
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 toFun
  deriv_ne_zero : ∀ t, deriv toFun t ≠ 0
  injOn : InjOn toFun (Ico 0 1)

instance : CoeFun Knot (fun _ ↦ ℝ → ℝ³) := ⟨Knot.toFun⟩

/-- Two knots `K₀` and `K₁` are *ambient isotopic* (have the same knot type) if there is a
continuous family `H t` (`t ∈ [0, 1]`) of homeomorphisms of `ℝ³` with `H 0 = id` and
`H 1` mapping the image of `K₀` onto the image of `K₁`. -/
def AmbientIsotopic (K₀ K₁ : Knot) : Prop :=
  ∃ H : C(unitInterval × ℝ³, ℝ³), (∀ x, H (0, x) = x) ∧ (∀ t, IsHomeomorph fun x ↦ H (t, x)) ∧
    (fun x ↦ H (1, x)) '' range K₀ = range K₁

lemma AmbientIsotopic.refl (K : Knot) : AmbientIsotopic K K :=
  ⟨⟨fun p ↦ p.2, continuous_snd⟩, fun _ ↦ rfl, fun _ ↦ IsHomeomorph.id, image_id _⟩

/-- The *thickness* of a knot `K`, in the sense of Gonzalez–Maddocks: the infimum of the
circumradius $r(x, y, z)$ over all triples of (non-collinear) distinct points `x y z` on `K`.
Collinear triples have infinite circumradius and hence do not contribute to the infimum.
For a $C^1$ curve this equals the radius of the largest embedded normal tube around `K`. -/
noncomputable def Knot.thickness (K : Knot) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (s : Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2) (_ : ∀ i, s.points i ∈ range K), ENNReal.ofReal s.circumradius

/-- The length of a knot `K`, i.e. the total variation of its parametrization over one period. -/
noncomputable def Knot.length (K : Knot) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  eVariationOn K (Icc 0 1)

/-- The *ropelength* of the curve `K`, i.e. the ratio of its length to its thickness
(measured in units of the tube radius). It is `∞` if the thickness is `0`. -/
noncomputable def Knot.curveRopelength (K : Knot) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  K.length / K.thickness

/-- The *ropelength* $\operatorname{Rop}(K)$ of the knot type of `K`: the infimum of the
ropelength over all knots ambient isotopic to `K`. -/
noncomputable def Knot.ropelength (K : Knot) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ (K' : Knot) (_ : AmbientIsotopic K K'), K'.curveRopelength

@[category API, AMS 51 57]
lemma Knot.ropelength_le_curveRopelength (K : Knot) : K.ropelength ≤ K.curveRopelength :=
  iInf₂_le K (AmbientIsotopic.refl K)

/-- A nonzero vector `v` is a *regular direction* for the knot `K` if the orthogonal projection
of `K` along `v` is a regular knot diagram: the projected curve is an immersion (no tangent of `K`
is parallel to `v`), no point of the plane is the projection of three distinct points of `K`, and
at every double point the two projected tangents are transverse. Here two points `K s` and `K t`
have the same projection if and only if `K s - K t ∈ ℝ ∙ v`. -/
structure IsRegularDirection (K : Knot) (v : ℝ³) : Prop where
  ne_zero : v ≠ 0
  deriv_notMem : ∀ t, deriv K t ∉ ℝ ∙ v
  no_triple_point : ∀ s ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ u ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1,
    s ≠ t → s ≠ u → t ≠ u → K s - K t ∈ ℝ ∙ v → K s - K u ∉ ℝ ∙ v
  transverse : ∀ s ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, ∀ t ∈ Ico (0 : ℝ) 1, s ≠ t → K s - K t ∈ ℝ ∙ v →
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![deriv K s, deriv K t, v]

/-- The crossings of the projection of the knot `K` along the direction `v`: the pairs of
parameters `s < t` in `[0, 1)` whose images have the same projection. -/
def crossings (K : Knot) (v : ℝ³) : Set (ℝ × ℝ) :=
  {p | p.1 ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ p.2 ∈ Ico 0 1 ∧ p.1 < p.2 ∧ K p.1 - K p.2 ∈ ℝ ∙ v}

/-- The *crossing number* $\operatorname{Cr}(K)$ of the knot type of `K`: the minimum number of
crossings of a regular diagram of a knot ambient isotopic to `K`. -/
noncomputable def Knot.crossingNumber (K : Knot) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n | ∃ K' : Knot, AmbientIsotopic K K' ∧
    ∃ v, IsRegularDirection K' v ∧ (crossings K' v).encard = n}

Is the minimum ropelength of a knot bounded above by a linear function of its crossing number?
That is, is there a universal constant $c$ such that
$\operatorname{Rop}(K) \leq c \operatorname{Cr}(K)$ for every nontrivial knot type $K$
(equivalently, $\operatorname{Rop}(K) = O(\operatorname{Cr}(K))$)?

\operatorname{Cr}(K))$, due to Diao, Ernst, Por and Ziegler. The unknot, which has crossing number
$0$ and ropelength $2\pi$, is excluded by the hypothesis $0 < \operatorname{Cr}(K)$. -/

    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ c : ℝ≥0, ∀ K : Knot, 0 < K.crossingNumber →

  sorry

Knot type is defined by ambient isotopy: a continuous H : [0,1] × ℝ³ → ℝ³ with H_0 = id, every H_t a homeomorphism (`IsHomeomorph`), and H_1 carrying the image of K₀ onto the image of K₁ (image equality, so knots are unoriented and reparametrization is irrelevant).

Thickness is the Gonzalez–Maddocks / Cantarella–Kusner–Sullivan definition: infimum over all triangles (`Affine.Simplex ℝ ℝ³ 2`, i.e. non-collinear triples) with vertices on the curve of the circumradius, in ℝ≥0∞. Collinear triples (radius ∞) are correctly omitted; the inf is never over an empty family for an embedded circle. This equals the normal injectivity radius (tube radius) for C^1 curves (CKS Lemma 2). Length is `eVariationOn K (Icc 0 1)` (total variation over one period, ℝ≥0∞). Curve ropelength is `length / thickness` in ℝ≥0∞: thickness 0 gives ropelength ⊤ (length is positive since the curve is non-constant), matching the convention that non-C^{1,1} curves have infinite ropelength, so no side condition τ > 0 is needed. Rop(K) is the ⨅ over the isotopy class (the 'minimum' of the article; minimizers exist by CKS but we do not rely on this).

A direction v ≠ 0 is regular if no tangent is parallel to v (projection is an immersion), no three distinct points project to the same point, and at each double point the projected tangents are transverse (encoded as `LinearIndependent ℝ ![K' s, K' t, v]` for the derivatives).   sSup {r : ℝ | 0 ≤ r ∧ ∀ x : E, Metric.infDist x (curveImage γ) < r →
    ∃! p : E, p ∈ curveImage γ ∧ dist x p = Metric.infDist x (curveImage γ)}

thickness. Restricting to positive thickness prevents division by zero in ropelength. -/

  toFun : ℝ → E
  contDiff : ContDiff ℝ 1 toFun
  periodic : Function.Periodic toFun 1
  injOn : Set.InjOn toFun (Ico 0 1)

ambient-isotopic realization. -/
noncomputable def crossingNumber (K : Knot) : ℕ :=
  sInf {n : ℕ | ∃ (L : Knot) (v : E), AmbientIsotopic K L ∧ IsRegularProjection L v ∧
    n = (projectionDoublePoints L v).ncard}

/-- A knot is an unknot when it is ambient isotopic to some planar round circle. -/
noncomputable def IsUnknot (K : Knot) : Prop :=
  ∃ L : Knot, AmbientIsotopic K L ∧ ∃ c : E, ∃ u w : E,
    LinearIndependent ℝ ![u, w] ∧ ‖u‖ = 1 ∧ ‖w‖ = 1 ∧ (inner ℝ u w) = 0 ∧
    ∀ t, L t = c + Real.cos (2 * Real.pi * t) • u + Real.sin (2 * Real.pi * t) • w

/--
Is the upper bound for the minimum ropelength of a closed knot linear in its crossing number?
Precisely: is there a universal positive constant $C$ such that every nontrivial tame closed knot
type $K$ satisfies $\operatorname{Rop}(K) \le C\operatorname{Cr}(K)$? Here ropelength is the
infimum of length divided by thickness over positive-thickness $C^1$ realizations, and crossing
number is minimized over regular projections. Nontrivial knots are used because the unknot has
crossing number zero but positive minimum ropelength.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem is_the_upper_bound_of_a_closed_knots_minimum_ropelength_linear_to_its_crossing :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ C : ℝ, 0 < C ∧ ∀ K : Knot, ¬ IsUnknot K →
      ropelength K ≤ C * crossingNumber K := by
  sorry

end IsTheUpperBoundOfAClosedKnotsMinimumRopelengthLinearToItsCrossing
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “linear upper bound” as the positive yes/no assertion that there is a universal constant C > 0 with Rop(K) ≤ C · Cr(K) for every nontrivial tame closed knot type.

Excluded the unknot rather than adding an additive constant, because the unknot has crossing number 0 and positive ropelength; this is one of the two boundary-case resolutions explicitly identified in the decomposition notes.

Represented tame knot types through regular one-periodic C¹ embeddings of the circle into Euclidean 3-space having positive thickness. Quantifying over representatives is equivalent to quantifying over represented knot types because ropelength and crossing number are minimized over the ambient-isotopy class.

Defined thickness as the reach of the curve image: the supremal radius within which every nearby ambient point has a unique nearest point on the curve. For regular closed curves this is the standard geometric thickness, equivalently the radius of the largest embedded normal tube.

Restricted admissible ropelength representatives to positive-thickness C¹ curves. This expresses the physical rope domain and prevents Lean’s totalized real division from assigning thickness-zero curves the spurious ratio Len/0 = 0.
Defined length as the integral over one period of the norm of the Fréchet derivative.
Defined ambient isotopy using jointly continuous families H and G of mutually inverse ambient maps, starting at the identity, with the endpoint carrying one curve image onto the other.

Defined crossing number by minimizing over ambient-isotopic realizations and regular orthogonal projections. Regularity requires a unit projection direction, finitely many crossings, no triple projected fibers, nonvanishing projected velocity, and transverse double points; each crossing is counted once by an ordered parameter pair t₁ < t₂.
Defined nontriviality geometrically: an unknot is ambient isotopic to an orthonormally parametrized planar round circle.
Used the radius convention for thickness. Changing to a diameter convention only rescales ropelength by a universal factor and does not change the linearity question.
